Liam: Quick heads-up 1: I'm doing a 6-week client sprint starting 2026-05-04. SF Mon/Tue, Vancouver Wed-Fri each week. Do I need to change homebase? How do we prorate the WFH stipend and any tax flags I should know about?

Sofia (People Ops): Short answer: no permanent homebase change for temporary trips under ~90 days; stipend prorated by days in-location; payroll will run withholding simulation for Canada. Please submit the Remote Work Request form and tick that payroll remains with Redwood.

Liam: Dates: 2026-05-04 -> 2026-06-12. Confirmed on Redwood payroll. Client site is Vancouver 1: does that modify the stipend rules (client office vs remote coworking)?

Marco (Payroll): Practically we treat client-site vs personal WFH the same for stipend proration, but client-site visits can increase nexus risk if multiple employees visit the same client/region repeatedly. For Canada: if total days in Canada exceed provincial thresholds or cumulative days across employees appear, local tax authorities may request payroll info. Please complete the form so I can run a withholding test: https://hr.redwood.example/forms/remote-request

Priya: Filing checklist for @Liam: 1) Remote Work Notification page in Confluence with week-by-week breakdown; 2) Attach itinerary and client contact; 3) Tag @Marco for payroll review. Stipend calculation we use: stipend_amount * (days_in_location / days_in_month) and we round to nearest dollar.

Sofia (People Ops): Example: monthly stipend $200, May portion if in Vancouver 3/31 days -> 200 * 3/31 = $19.35, rounded on payroll. We handle currency conversion and display both USD and CAD amounts on your pay stub.

people-ops-bot: Remote Request submitted by Liam 1: Request ID RR-2026-451 (status: pending payroll review).

Liam: Thanks. Any change to benefits or medical coverage while in Canada for 6 weeks?

Priya: Your US benefits remain primary for travel under ~90 days. If you incur medical expenses in Canada, keep itemized receipts and mark as travel-related on claims. If you plan to stay longer than ~3 months or enroll dependents domestically in Canada, we will need to revisit benefits and possibly enroll in local plans.

Marco (Payroll): One operational note: confirm the weekly pattern per calendar week (e.g., Mon/Tue SF, Wed-Fri YVR) so I can test multi-jurisdiction payroll rules. Also flag if other Redwood employees will be at the same client site; multiple employees visiting the same customer in a jurisdiction over time can create a tax nexus trigger and require legal sign-off.

Liam: I added the week-by-week schedule to the form and attached the client contact. RR-2026-451. Quick Q: Is there a limit on the number of short stints per year?

Sofia (People Ops): No strict cap. Operational rule: more than 6 months cumulative in a rolling 12-month window triggers a homebase and payroll review. If multiple short trips across employees create risk, we'll coordinate with Legal and Finance. :thumbsup:

Liam: Appreciate it 1: I'll keep receipts and update if dates change. Thanks everyone!
